(Los Angeles, California) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (2020–2021) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2020]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2020) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2020) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 Greece]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Ziaire Williams''' (born September 12, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]]. ==Early life== Williams was born in [[Lancaster, California]] as the only child of Ziaire Williams and Marquita Fields-Williams.{{cite web |title=Ziaire Williams |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/williams-ziaire.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=July 23, 2019 |date=July 22, 2019}} He began playing basketball at age five and was training under the guidance of his father by age eight.{{cite web |last1=Abeytia |first1=R. J. |title=Stanford '20 Offer Ziaire Williams Keeps Perspective |url=https://247sports.com/college/stanford/LongFormArticle/Stanford-20-Offer-Ziaire-Williams-Keeps-Perspective-128730914/#128730914_1 |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=July 23, 2019 |date=February 5, 2019}} ==High school career== For his first three years of high school, Williams attended [[Notre Dame High School (Sherman Oaks, California)|Notre Dame High School]] in [[Sherman Oaks, Los Angeles]]. In his freshman season, he averaged 13.6 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Ugland |first1=Devin |title=Recruiting Report: Ziaire Williams (2020) |url=https://www.prephoops.com/2017/08/recruiting-report-ziaire-williams-2020/ |publisher=Prep Hoops |access-date=July 23, 2019 |date=August 4, 2017}} Williams missed much of his sophomore season with an injury but saw success in the summer with his club team BTI Select.{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=Skilled wing Ziaire Williams making waves in 2020 |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/skilled-wing-ziaire-williams-making-waves-in-2020 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=July 24, 2019 |date=June 1, 2018}} On January 14, 2019, as a junior, he was named ''[[Los Angeles Daily News]]'' boys athlete of the week following two consecutive games with at least 34 points.{{cite web |last1=Fattal |first1=Tarek |title=Daily News Boys Athlete of the Week: Ziaire Williams, Notre Dame |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/14/daily-news-boys-athlete-of-the-week-ziaire-williams-notre-dame/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=July 24, 2019 |date=January 14, 2019}} In his junior season, Williams averaged 27 points, 10 rebounds, and three assists per game. He earned All-[[Mission League]] first team and ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA California second team honors.{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=Johnny Juzang is Mission League MVP |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vti-all-mission-league-20190227-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=July 24, 2019 |date=February 27, 2019}}{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA California Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2018-19-all-usa-california-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 24, 2019 |date=April 16, 2019}} On July 18, 2019, Williams transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles]] for his [[Senior (education)|senior]] year. He joined the team with fellow five-star recruit [[BJ Boston]], as well as [[Bronny James]] and Zaire Wade, the respective sons of basketball players [[LeBron James]] and [[Dwyane Wade]].{{cite web |last1=Fattal |first1=Tarek |title=Ziaire Williams transferring from Notre Dame to Sierra Canyon |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2019/07/18/ziaire-williams-transferring-from-notre-dame-to-sierra-canyon/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |access-date=July 24, 2019 |date=July 18, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Rollins |first1=Khadrice |title=Five-Star Recruit BJ Boston Joining Ziaire Williams, Bronny at Sierra Canyon |url=https://www.si.com/high-school/2019/07/20/sierra-canyon-bj-boston-five-star-recruit-ziaire-williams-lebron-james-jr |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 24, 2019 |date=July 20, 2019}} Williams was not eligible to play until December 29, due to [[CIF Southern Section]] (CIF-SS) transfer rules, and missed more than 10 games.{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Logan |title=Five-star SF Ziaire Williams won't be eligible for Sierra Canyon until Dec. 29 |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/ziaire-williams-ineligible-sierra-canyon-until-dec-29 |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=April 12, 2020 |date=October 30, 2019}} In his season debut, he scored 28 points in an 85–81 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss to Rancho Christian School.{{cite web |last1=Fattal |first1=Tarek |title=Evan Mobley, Rancho Christian spoil Ziaire Williams’ debut, give Sierra Canyon its first loss |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/12/30/evan-mobley-rancho-christian-spoil-ziaire-williams-debut-gives-sierra-canyon-first-loss/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=April 12, 2020 |date=December 30, 2019}} On March 11, 2020, Williams scored 17 points and made a buzzer-beater in a 63–61 comeback win over [[Etiwanda High School]].{{cite web |last1=Kasabian |first1=Paul |title=Ziaire Williams Caps Comeback to Lead Bronny, Zaire, Sierra Canyon over Etiwanda |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2880305-bronny-james-zaire-wade-sierra-canyon-use-wild-comeback-to-beat-etiwanda |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=April 12, 2020 |date=March 11, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 15 points, 7.9 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game, helping Sierra Canyon win the CIF-SS Open Division title. He was named player of the year by the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]''.{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=The Times' boys' basketball player of the year: Ziaire Williams |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/story/2020-03-28/the-times-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-ziaire-williams |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=April 12, 2020 |date=March 28, 2020}} Williams was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but all three games were canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=June 17, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Williams was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the number one [[small forward]] in the 2020 recruiting class. On April 12, 2020, he announced his commitment to [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. Williams became Stanford's highest-ranked recruit in the modern recruiting era and the program's first five-star recruit since [[Reid Travis]] in 2014.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Forward Ziaire Williams, ranked No. 7 in ESPN 100, commits to Stanford |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29026645/forward-ziaire-williams-ranked-no-7-espn-100-commits-stanford |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 12, 2020 |date=April 12, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Gershon |first1=Josh |title=Evaluating No. 5 Stanford commit Ziaire Williams |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Stanford-basketball-recruiting-Ziaire-Williams-commitment-evaluation-145978380/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=April 12, 2020 |date=April 12, 2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Ziaire Williams | position = [[Small forward|SF]] | hometown = [[Lancaster, California|Lancaster, CA]] | highschool = [[Sierra Canyon School|Sierra Canyon]] (CA) | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = April 12, 2020 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 95 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Stanford 2020 Basketball Commitments | espn ref title = 2020 Stanford Cardinal Recruiting Class | rivals school = stanford | espn schoolid = 24 | 247 overall = 5 | rivals overall = 6 | espn overall = 8 | access-date = August 19, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In his collegiate debut for Stanford on November 30, 2020, Williams scored 19 points and grabbed eight rebounds in an 82–64 win against [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite news |title=Williams boosts Stanford; sets up showdown with Tar Heels |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401255065 |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 30, 2020}} On January 7, 2021, he recorded 12 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists, the first [[triple-double]] by a Stanford player since 2007, in a 91–75 victory over [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].{{cite web |title=Williams' Triple Double Leads Cardinal Rout of Washington |url=https://gostanford.com/news/2021/1/7/mens-basketball-williams-triple-double-leads-cardinal-rout-of-washington.aspx |website=Stanford Athletics |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 20, 2021 |date=January 7, 2021}} As a freshman, Williams averaged 10.7 points, 4.6 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game, shooting 37.4 percent from the field. On March 31, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=Stanford's Ziaire Williams Declares for 2021 NBA Draft; Averaged 10.7 PPG |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2933404-stanfords-ziaire-williams-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-averaged-107-ppg |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=March 31, 2021}} ==National team career== Williams played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. In seven games, he averaged 5.3 points and 1.2 assists per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Ziaire Williams (USA)'s profile - FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2019/player/Ziaire-Williams |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=July 24, 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]] | 20 || 14 || 27.9 || .374 || .291 || .796 || 4.6 || 2.2 || .9 || .6 || 10.7 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Both of Williams' parents have served in the military: his mother, Marquita Fields-Williams, in the [[United States Army|Army]] and [[United States Air Force|Air Force]], and his father, Ziaire Williams, in the [[United States Marine Corps|Marine Corps]]. His mother is a [[probation officer]], and his father works for [[7 Up]] in [[Sylmar, Los Angeles]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://gostanford.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ziaire-williams/17103 Stanford Cardinal bio] *[https://sierracanyonathletics.com/player/ziaire-williams/ Sierra Canyon Trailblazers bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/williams-ziaire.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Williams, Ziaire}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:People from Lancaster, California]] [[Category:Sierra Canyon School alumni]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Stanford Cardinal men's basketball players]]
